summary: Verified the ProjectUpdateReview stale-compose regression fix. Full flow tested on /project/222535e8-18f0-403d-b62f-d0048acbbc72 as support@use-bracket.com: banner Review opens project-update-drawer (PROJECT CHANGE), Accept transitions to update-compose, Skip closes, and re-triggering the modal no longer shows the stale 'Send your client an update' compose screen — it correctly shows the caught-up empty state (all pending items were consumed in the single Accept, which is an accepted pass per the review request).
critical_code_review_comments: Fix at ProjectUpdateReview.jsx L57 is correct: setCompose(null); setDraft('') added to the open-effect. Both close paths (update-compose-skip and update-compose-close) call the same onClose, so the same effect covers both. No further changes needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: ProjectUpdateReview stale-compose bug is FIXED and verified. On project 222535e8-18f0-403d-b62f-d0048acbbc72 the banner (data-testid=change-banner-review) bundles all 14 pending changes into ONE update; a single Accept consumes all of them, so the banner disappears afterwards and reopening the modal via the header bell (data-testid=header-bell) yields the calm 'You're all caught up' state (project-update-empty) rather than the stale update-compose. The X-close path could not be exercised on this project because there were no more pending changes after the first Accept, but it is guaranteed by the same open-effect reset (setCompose(null); setDraft('')) since update-compose-close and update-compose-skip both invoke the same onClose handler.
rca of the issue: Root cause was in ProjectUpdateReview.jsx open-effect (L55-71): it reset update/none/removed but not compose/draft. So if the user Accepted (which sets compose), then closed via Skip or X, the local compose state persisted. Next time open flipped from false→true, the render short-circuit at L138 (`if (compose) return composeModal`) fired before the build POST completed, showing the stale compose screen. Fix adds setCompose(null); setDraft('') to the reset line, ensuring reopen always starts from a fresh review/loading/empty state.
